# C# and .NET library guidance

- CS-001: Don't use _ = Task.Run(...) or _ = SomeAsyncMethod() to discard a task in application code; await the task.
- CS-002: Prefer the shorter _ discard pattern for a switch catch-all, and avoid declaring your own variables, constants or types named _.
- CS-003: Prefer raw string literals over verbatim (@) strings in new code.
- CS-004: Avoid dynamic in most application code.
- CS-005: Including an explanation of what to use instead in an Obsolete attribute is recommended.
- CS-006: Outside the initialization code source generators need, in most cases you should write a static constructor instead of a module initializer; and library authors should use OverloadResolutionPriority as a last resort when adding a new and better method overload.
- CS-007: Almost always define a member with value 0 in an enum.
- CS-008: Computed properties in record types should be computed on access, not initialized when the instance is created.
- CS-009: Defining immutable structure types is recommended, and if you're focused on the behavior of a type, consider defining a class.
- CS-010: For a by-reference struct parameter, prefer ref readonly over in when the method captures the parameter or returns it by readonly reference.
- CS-011: Avoid using stackalloc inside loops, and never give it a negative length: where the length comes from user input, forbid negative values and cap the maximum.
- CS-012: Starting with .NET 9 and C# 13, lock a dedicated System.Threading.Lock instance for best performance (on an older .NET and C#, a dedicated object instance that isn't used for another purpose); avoid using the same lock object instance for different shared resources; and avoid this, Type instances and string instances (including string literals) as lock objects.
- CS-013: Don't block the current thread in static constructors and initializers: don't wait on tasks, threads, wait handles or events, don't acquire locks, and don't run blocking parallel operations there.
- CS-014: Subscribing to an event with an anonymous function is not recommended if you have to unsubscribe from it later, and you should unsubscribe from events before you dispose of a subscriber object.
- CS-015: Don't call a method in a LINQ query expression that can create a side effect, such as modifying the data source or throwing an exception; and don't mix declarative and imperative code when you query and modify a LINQ to XML tree.
- CS-016: For a class library you implemented, you should not use extension methods to avoid incrementing the assembly's version number; to add significant functionality to a library whose source code you own, follow the .NET guidelines for assembly versioning.
- CS-017: Avoid declaring a new method with the same name as a virtual method of a base class.
- CS-018: Avoid overriding the same method in multiple derived interfaces.
- CS-019: A method whose arguments could be null, and are known to be not null when it returns true, should be annotated with NotNullWhen.
- CS-020: The recommended way to deal with the platform compatibility analyzer's diagnostics is to make sure you only call platform-specific APIs when running on an appropriate platform; suppressing the warning should be a last resort.
- CS-021: In a library, don't expose asynchronous methods purely for offloading, and don't expose a synchronous method that wraps an asynchronous implementation: leave the choice to offload, and the decision whether to block, to the consumer.
- CS-022: When you complete a task by hand (a TaskCompletionSource), always complete it in success and failure paths; and when work must continue after the caller returns, transfer ownership of it explicitly.
- CS-023: If you can use the regular expression source generator, use it; prefer it when you use Regex in C# with arguments known at compile time.
- CS-024: Validate an email address with a small regular expression that checks its structure, never with a regular expression alone, and send a test email to the address a user gives.
- CS-025: If you can choose the encoding, you should use a Unicode encoding, preferably UTF8Encoding or UnicodeEncoding, and you should use UTF-8 instead of UTF-7 if possible; most new applications should avoid best-fit behavior; whenever possible, you should specify an encoding object's fallback strategy when you instantiate it; and the encoding classes should not be used to store binary data in string form: to convert binary data to a string form, use Convert.ToBase64String.
- CS-026: When you implement the observer pattern, don't write observers that depend on being notified before or after another observer, don't throw exceptions from OnNext or OnError, and the recommended pattern is to attach an observer to only one provider.
- CS-027: Using the cooperative cancellation model for all new library and application code is recommended; you should call CancellationTokenSource.Dispose when you have finished using the cancellation token source; and library code that provides cancelable operations should also provide public methods that accept an external cancellation token.
- CS-028: Don't assume that parallel is always faster: always measuring actual results is recommended; avoiding, or at least limiting, access to shared state in a parallel loop is recommended; one iteration of a parallel loop should never wait on another iteration of the loop to make progress; catching an AggregateException without observing any of its inner exceptions is not recommended; and source.AsParallel().Where().ForAll(...) should be strongly preferred to Parallel.ForEach(source.AsParallel().Where(), ...).
- CS-029: Avoid using weak references as an automatic solution to memory management problems (develop an effective caching policy instead) and avoid weak references to small objects; allocating a pool of large objects that you reuse instead of allocating temporary ones is recommended; and an app should never make assumptions about or depend on a particular garbage collector segment size.
- CS-030: When extracting an untrusted ZIP or TAR archive, always enforce limits on decompressed size and entry count, applications should check that extracted entry names conform to an acceptable pattern, and don't use ExtractToDirectory (iterate the entries manually); when creating encrypted ZIP entries, always prefer Aes256.
- CS-031: If you must process untrusted XML from unknown sources, using an XmlReader configured to filter out known XML denial-of-service attacks is recommended; you should not accept DTDs or XSD schemas from untrusted sources; and error messages should not be exposed to callers that aren't trusted: you should catch all errors and report them with your own custom error messages.
- CS-032: Prefer RSA over DSA, and prefer SHA-2 (SHA256, SHA384, SHA512) over MD5 and SHA-1.
- CS-033: Use System.Text.Json source generation in Native AOT apps.
- CS-038: When you use System.IO.Pipelines, always complete the PipeReader and PipeWriter (including an exception where applicable), and always call AdvanceTo after ReadAsync.
- CS-039: When you marshal native structures, avoid using classes to express complex native types through inheritance, and use InlineArray to define fixed-size buffers in modern .NET (C# 12 and later).
